## Instructions

Part 1. Draw the line y=4x+3 on a plot that ranges from -20 to +20 on both x and y. Label the line appropriately next to itself. Color the line in an interesting color! And make it dashed. Bonus Use a combination of the above options (plus others, if you feel like looking them up) to create the wildest looking series of lines on a graph that you can. (Remember, you can overplot lines!)

# Part 1.

```{r}
graphics.off()

plot(x=0,type='n',xlim=c(-20,20), ylim=c(-20,20),xlab = "X",ylab="Y",main = "Drawing an IMPORTANT line ")

abline(a=3,
  b=4,
  col="seagreen3",
  lwd=3,
  lty="dashed")

text(5,8,"y=4x+3",col = "black")


```

Part 2. Protected Lands Consider the protected_lands.csv dataset. This dataset contains information about a sample of countries sourced from the World Bank. Protected Lands represents the terrestrial protected land of a country as a percentage of total land area. GDP is represented in the dataset on a per capita (gdp_percap) as well as total basis (with total being measured in billions - tot_gdp_billions).

Find the mean, standard deviation, and range of each of the three variables: protected lands, GDP per capita, and total GDP.

Create a scatterplot where “protected lands” is on the Y axis and GDP per capita is on the X axis. Place a title on the graph and labels on the X and Y axis appropriately.

Create a scatterplot where “protected lands” is on the Y axis and total GDP is on the X axis. Place a title on the graph and labels on the X and Y axis appropriately.

Regress “protected lands” on GDP per capita.

Create a scatterplot where “protected lands” is on the Y axis and GDP per capita is on the X axis. Then, overlay the plot with a best fit line.

Regress “protected land” on total GDP.

Create a scatterplot where “protected lands” is on the Y axis and total GDP is on the X axis. Then, overlay the plot with a best fit line.

# Part 2.

```{r}
#1
graphics.off()
df <- data <- read.csv("~/Downloads/PAI 741/Data Sets/protected_lands.csv")


#mean, standard deviation, and range
mean(df$protected_lands)
sd(df$protected_lands)
range(df$protected_lands)

mean(df$gdp_percap)
sd(df$gdp_percap)
range(df$gdp_percap)

mean(df$tot_gdp_bilions)
sd(df$tot_gdp_bilions)
range(df$tot_gdp_bilions)

```

```{r}
# 2
plot(df$gdp_percap, df$protected_lands,
     main = "Protected Lands vs GDP per Capita",
     xlab = "GDP per Capita", 
     ylab = "Protected Lands (%)")
```

```{r}
# 3
plot(df$tot_gdp_bilions, df$protected_lands,
     main = "Protected Lands vs Total GDP",
     xlab = "Total GDP (Billions)", 
     ylab = "Protected Lands (%)")

```

```{r}
# 4
model1 <- lm(protected_lands ~ gdp_percap, data = df)
summary(model1)

```

```{r}
#5
plot(df$gdp_percap, df$protected_lands,
     main = "Protected Lands vs GDP per Capita",
     xlab = "GDP per Capita", 
     ylab = "Protected Lands (%)")
abline(model1)
```

```{r}
# 6
model2 <- lm(protected_lands ~ tot_gdp_bilions, data = df)
summary(model2)

```

```{r}
# 7
plot(df$tot_gdp_bilions, df$protected_lands,
     main = "Protected Lands vs Total GDP",
     xlab = "Total GDP (Billions)", ylab = "Protected Lands (%)")
abline(model2)
```
